rotation_concept_study.question: on-deck rotation or rocking of a SEALED plate about a horizontal axis, loaded by the gripper (2024 evidence: plate on edge on a rotator kept beads better than vigorous flat shaking)
rotation_concept_study.concept: a cradle (two side jaws closing on the plate's long sides, like the gripper) on a horizontal shaft along X under a deck position, turned by a geared NEMA17 through +/-90 deg (rocking) or 360 deg (end over end); the gripper sets the sealed plate flat into the open cradle at the top of its swing, the jaws close, the cradle rotates; it returns flat and opens for the gripper
rotation_concept_study.space: a 128 x 86 plate turning about its long axis sweeps a 128 x 86 diameter cylinder (86 mm): with the axis 50 mm above the deck it needs z 7..93 over the position and the two neighbours' edges in Y kept clear: it takes one position and the rows beside it must hold low labware only
rotation_concept_study.sealing: the plate must be sealed liquid-tight (heat seal or adhesive film): the gripper lid LD-1 does not seal; heat sealing is not on the deck (ADR-006: plate sealer not found cheaply) - so each rotation needs a manual seal, which defeats the purpose unless a cap-mat or clamped silicone lid that the gripper can fit is proven leak-tight
rotation_concept_study.amateur_build: the mechanics (shaft, two bearings, a geared stepper, printed jaws, a home switch) are within an amateur's reach; the leak-tight closure the gripper can place is NOT, and it is the deciding risk
rotation_concept_study.verdict: feasible as mechanics, NOT feasible as an automated step until a gripper-placed leak-tight closure exists; first test on the bench rig: orbital shaking at low speed on the shaker (ADR-006 consequence 1) before building a rotator
rotation_concept_study.cost_estimate: about GBP 80-150 of bought parts (stepper + gearbox, bearings, shaft, switch) plus printed jaws (ESTIMATE)

shaker.lid_park: D3: LD-1 parks on top of the TC-1 sealing lid on the LS-1 pedestal (two lids, last on first off, rule K-L1)
